newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-AUSTRALIA NOTCH WIN AGAINST OPPENHEIMER XI.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-AUSTRALIA NOTCH WIN AGAINST OPPENHEIMER XI.

text.p: Australia began their tour of South Africa with a typically relaxed fixture against diamond magnate Nicky Oppenheimer's invitation XI at his private ground at Randjesfontein outside Johannesburg on Thursday.
The tourists beat a mixture of up-and-coming and retired players by 19 runs in a one-day game with no over limitations.

Australia batted first and added 124 for the first wicket with Matthew Hayden and Matthew Elliot both easily passing the fifty mark. Hayden's 60 came from 65 balls with five fours and two sixes, while Elliot's 91 took 106 balls with four fours and fou sixes.
But the late impetus came from Steve Waugh who retired having made 72 from just 44 deliveries with nine fours and two sixes.
Mark Taylor declared at 284 for six after 55.1 overs and Australia seemed well set for victory when the invitation XI slumped to 114 for five after seamer Paul Reiffel quickly removed both openers.
But 21 year-old Neil McKenzie, son of former Springbok Kevin McKenzie, struck a brilliant 133 from just 121 balls with 19 boundaries and a six to lift the total to 265.

The Invitation XI's last wicket pair survived until the days penultimate ball when captain Jonathon Oppenheimer, Nicky's son, edged left arm spinner Michael Bevan to Justin Langer who had taken over from Ian Healy behind the stumps.
Australia begin their campaign in earnest on Saturday against reigning first class champions Western Province at Newlands in Cape Town.
